history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN (DIGAMBARA) TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Kohima Jain Temple, on Kohima-Mokokchung Road, is the oldest Jain temple in Nagaland (and described as the oldest in North East India), established in 1920 by eight Sethi families whose patriarchs were Shri Hardeo Sethi and Shri Hiralal Sethi - among the first non-Naga settlers in Nagaland. The Moolnayak (principal idol) is of Mahavira. The families moved to Dimapur in 1944 during the Japanese invasion in World War II and later built the Dimapur Jain Temple (1947), SD Jain School (1947) and SD Jain Charitable Hospital (1975). The temple marked its centenary in 2021; the then president of the Kohima Jain Temple Committee was Shri Pawan Kumar Sethi. Address: Shri Digambar Jain Mandir, Kohima-Mokokchung Road, Kohima 797001. Only a signboard photo is verified on Wikimedia Commons; no verified photo of the temple building was found, so media is empty.

town_description: Kohima is the capital of Nagaland, a hill city at about 1,444 m above sea level. It is famous for the 1944 Battle of Kohima and the Kohima War Cemetery, and hosts the annual Hornbill Festival at nearby Kisama. Jains form a tiny (~0.1%) but long-established trading community in Nagaland, concentrated mostly in Dimapur today.
